documents.title: Office visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First in-person visit in a year. Both covid shots done, felt lousy for a day after #2.

No complaints. Walking most days. Sugars 110-140 fasting. Home BP 130s/80s. No bleeding, no chest pain or dyspnea, no claudication.

Exam: Wt 95 kg, a little down. Heart irreg irreg, rate 70s. Lungs clear. No edema.

Labs: A1c 6.7. Cr/K fine. INR in range.

A/P:
- DM2: good, continue metformin 1000 BID.
- HTN: at goal, lisinopril/HCTZ.
- AF, warfarin: stable INRs, keep monthly-ish draws.
- HLD/PAD: statin, aspirin. Lipids at AWV.
- Obesity: slow progress.
AWV in Sept.

Feels well, no concerns today. Eye exam in August normal, no retinopathy. No falls, no hospital stays. Still drives, does his own yard. PHQ-2 0. Advance directive forms still at home, unsigned; nudged.

1. DM2 - continue metformin.
2. HTN - controlled.
3. AF on warfarin / prior stroke - stable, cardiology yearly.
4. HLD, PAD - atorvastatin 40, aspirin.
5. Lung screening - due Nov, ordered.
6. Flu next month; covid booster when eligible, pharmacy is fine.
RTC 6 months.

orders.reason: Pulsatile periumbilical mass; father with ruptured AAA

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit. He has nothing to bring up today and feels well.

Interval: no ED visits or hospital stays. Eye exam July, no retinopathy. Still walking. No falls. PHQ-2 0.

Meds unchanged: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 12.5, metoprolol succ 50, warfarin 5 per INR, ASA 81, atorvastatin 40, omeprazole 20. NKDA.

Family hx reviewed - father died of a ruptured AAA at 72; mother DM2 and macular degeneration; paternal uncle Waldenstrom; brother HTN.
Social: quit smoking 2017 after his stroke, 40 pk-yr. Wine with dinner.

Vitals: BP 142/88, HR 78, BMI 29.

Exam: Pleasant, NAD. Heart irregularly irregular, no murmur, no carotid or abdominal bruits. Lungs clear. Abdomen: nontender, but there is a pulsatile mass just above the umbilicus. Peripheral pulses intact. No leg edema. Feet intact, monofilament normal.

Fasting labs 8/5: TC 180, HDL 45, LDL 100, TG 175. Fasting glucose 98. A1c, CMP, CBC, UACR otherwise unremarkable. INR in range.

A/P:
1. Pulsatile abdominal mass - concerning for AAA, especially with his father's history and smoking. Aortic ultrasound ordered, asked them to fit him in next week. Talked through what it might mean.
2. T2DM - good control, continue metformin.
3. HTN - 142/88 today, home readings lower. Recheck next visit.
4. AF/warfarin, prior stroke - stable.
5. HLD/PAD - LDL 100 on atorvastatin 40, continue.
6. Lung screening due in fall.
RTC after the ultrasound.

reports.text:
EXAM: Ultrasound of the abdominal aorta.
INDICATION: Pulsatile periumbilical mass. Family history of ruptured AAA.
FINDINGS: The proximal abdominal aorta is normal in caliber. The infrarenal abdominal aorta is aneurysmal, measuring 4.8 cm in maximal outer-to-outer diameter. The aneurysm ends above the bifurcation. Common iliac arteries are normal in caliber.

documents.title: Ultrasound result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with aortic US: infrarenal AAA 4.8 cm. Explained this is below the size where repair is routine, but with his father's rupture he should see vascular surgery now to talk through surveillance vs repair. He wants to be seen. Referral placed, sent US images and note. Reviewed warning signs - sudden severe abdominal or back pain, fainting - call 911. Keep BP controlled; stays off cigarettes.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
EXAM: CT angiography of the abdomen and pelvis.
INDICATION: Infrarenal AAA on ultrasound, pre-procedure planning.
FINDINGS: Fusiform infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm with maximal diameter 4.8 cm. Infrarenal neck of adequate length and diameter for endograft seal. Common and external iliac arteries normal in caliber and patent. Atherosclerotic changes of the aorta and iliac arteries. Renal arteries single and patent. Visualized organs unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: 4.8 cm infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm; anatomy suitable for endovascular repair.

documents.title: Vascular surgery consultation
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE VASCULAR SURGERY - new patient consultation. Date of service 09/06/2022.

Reason: infrarenal AAA found on exam and ultrasound by his primary care physician.

Mr. Rossi is a 68 year old retired foreman with AF on warfarin, prior mild ischemic stroke, hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia and mild PAD. Asymptomatic: no abdominal or back pain. Former 40 pack-year smoker. His father died of a ruptured AAA at 72, which weighs heavily on him.

Medications: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, metoprolol succinate, warfarin, aspirin, atorvastatin, omeprazole. Allergies: none known.

Exam: Pulsatile, nontender supraumbilical mass. Femoral pulses palpable bilaterally. Distal pulses present.

CTA 9/2: fusiform infrarenal AAA 4.8 cm, good neck, iliacs normal caliber - favorable for EVAR. Creatinine 1.0.

Assessment and plan: 4.8 cm infrarenal AAA. We discussed that in men repair is usually offered at 5.5 cm and that surveillance imaging every 6-12 months is reasonable. Given his strong family history and his own preference after a long discussion, we will proceed with elective EVAR, scheduled 9/26. Hold warfarin 5 days before (last dose 9/20), no bridging needed; continue aspirin. Hold metformin the day of the procedure. Plan to resume warfarin the day after.

Thank you for this referral.

documents.title: Warfarin hold for EVAR
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Reviewed the vascular surgeon's instructions with pt: last warfarin 9/20, no warfarin 9/21-9/25, keep aspirin, no metformin morning of 9/26. Surgery team restarts warfarin. INR here about a week after he restarts. Wrote it out on a calendar for him and he read it back.

procedures.procedure: Endovascular repair of infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm with bifurcated endograft

documents.title: Discharge summary - EVAR
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HOSPITAL DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 09/26/2022, discharged 09/27/2022. Service: Vascular Surgery.

Procedure 09/26/2022: endovascular repair of infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm with bifurcated stent graft, bilateral percutaneous femoral access with closure devices. Completion angiography: graft widely patent, no endoleak.

Course: uneventful. Groins without hematoma, distal pulses present. Tolerating diet, ambulating, voiding.

Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medications: resume warfarin 5 mg daily starting 9/27; resume metformin 1000 mg twice daily; continue aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, omeprazole 20 mg.

Follow-up: vascular surgery clinic with duplex in 6-8 weeks. INR check with primary care within a week. Call for groin swelling, leg pain or color change, abdominal or back pain.

documents.title: Post-procedure call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Post-discharge call after EVAR. Feels well, a little groin soreness both sides, no swelling or bleeding at the puncture sites. Eating fine. Back on warfarin since 9/27. Lab draw for INR booked 10/4.

documents.title: INR
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR 1.6 a week after restarting after the procedure hold. Expected. Per protocol 7.5 mg tonight and tomorrow, then 5 mg daily. Recheck at his visit.
